gaps.needs: For every field K and rational fan, supply toric schemes glued from Spec K[σ∨∩M], the dense torus, face/orbit charts, toric morphisms, equivariant products and the closed-graph domination of toric embeddings needed in §§4.1–4.4 and §§5.2–5.6.

For proper flat admissible normal models over any complete nontrivially valued rank-one valuation ring, supply specialization of generic intersection degree to component-weighted residue-field intersections, retaining tensor denominators, residue degrees and nonreduced multiplicities, for §6.2.

For those rank-one models, supply vertical Cartier intersection and projection under proper admissible modifications, compatibility with isometric scalar extension and common refinements, for §§6.2, 6.7 and 6.8.

For isometric embeddings of complete real absolute-valued fields F into K and L, supply a common complete absolute-valued field with isometric embeddings of K and L agreeing on F, including trivial and archimedean valuations, for §§0.16 and 0.18; valuation equivalence alone is insufficient.

Extend the supplied nonarchimedean completed-tensor injectivity and faithful scalar-extension interfaces to trivially valued complete base fields, including injectivity B⊗_K L→B⊗̂_K L for Banach K-spaces and faithful extension of finite affinoid modules, for §§0.18–0.20.

For an abelian variety with split semistable reduction over any complete nontrivially valued rank-one field, supply the analytic Raynaud cross 0→M′→Eᵃⁿ→Aᵃⁿ→0 and 0→T→E→B→0 with B of good reduction and compatibility with isometric base extension and descent, for §7.5.
For that Raynaud cross, supply trop:Eᵃⁿ→N_ℝ, its good-reduction kernel on valued points, its full period lattice trop(M′), and scalar-extension/descent compatibility, for §§7.5 and 7.8.

For that cross with principal polarization, supply the multiplicative period/monodromy pairing, its valuation pairing and scalar-extension descent over arbitrary complete rank-one bases, for comparison with the skeleton length pairing in §7.5.
